title: BA1/1295/2013 of Major Singh Vs State Of Uttarakhand

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
ORIGINAL JURISDICTION
First Bail Application No. 1295 of 2013
Order on the Bail application of accused.
CRIMINAL SIDE
Major Singh S/o Sri Suchha Singh,
Resident of village-Herherpur,
Bahura, Pargana Rich,
Tehsil-Baheri,
District Bareilly (U.P.) ............ Applicant (In Jail)
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ...........Respondent
Arising out of F.I.R./Crime No. 549 of 2011,
Under Section 420, 467, 468 and 471 I.P.C..
Police Station Rudrapur,
District Pauri Udham Singh Nagar.
Dated: October 29, 2013
Hon'ble V.K. Bist J.
Mr. Lalit Sharma, advocate for the accused/
applicant.
Mr. M.A. Khan, A.G.A. with Ms. Sangeeta Miyan,
Brief Holder for the State.
Heard learned counsel for the parties.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted
that the alleged loan which has been shown to have been
taken by the applicant in the year 2007, was never taken
by the applicant for the said Bank either in cash or in the
form of cheque and draft. It is further submitted that
when the applicant came to know about the same, he
himself filed complaint before the higher authorities on
23.12.2010 and only thereafter, the alleged First
Information Report was registered. The applicant
cooperated in the investigation and was never arrested by
the police. It is then contended that the applicant himself
surrendered on 03.10.2013. It is further submitted that
the F.I.R. has been lodged after a belated stage of 4 years

2
9 months and the delay has not been explained in the
F.I.R. It is submitted that the applicant has no criminal or
bad antecedents and the entire proceeding is the outcome
of civil litigation. Counsel for the applicant then
submitted that the applicant undertakes that if he is
enlarged on bail, he will be abide by the terms and
conditions of the bail.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and
upon examining the material available on record, without
expressing any opinion about the merits of the case, this
Court is of the view that the applicant deserves bail at this
stage.
Let the accuse/applicant Major Singh be released on
bail on his executing a personal bond of ` 25,000/- and
furnishing two sureties each in the like amount to the
satisfaction of C.J.M. concerned.
The first bail application disposed of accordingly.
 (V.K. Bist, J.)
 29.x.2013
